answer.label: Attributed to
answer.authorDates: b. 1934 · American feminist writer, journalist & activist
answer.sourceLine: The line is near-universally credited to Gloria Steinem and reads as authentically hers — it is the tail of a two-sentence thought, “Without leaps of imagination, or dreaming, we lose the excitement of possibilities. Dreaming, after all, is a form of planning.” It is often associated with her 1992 book Revolution from Within, but no source I could check — Quote Investigator, Wikiquote’s sourced section, or the quotation archives — pins the exact wording to a specific page, essay, or date. So: firmly attributed, not yet verified to a primary source.
answer.confidenceText: Attributed to Gloria Steinem — widely credited and consistent with her work, but no primary source is documented.

source.excerpt: Without leaps of imagination, or dreaming, we lose the excitement of possibilities. Dreaming, after all, is a form of planning.
trail: The line circulates everywhere credited to Steinem — e.g. Goodreads ↗ carries the fuller two-sentence form, but flags that quotes are user-added and are “not verified,” and cites no book.
Good Good Good ↗’s roundup of Steinem quotes reproduces the full sentence and, like every other aggregator, attaches no source work or date.
Wikiquote ↗’s Steinem page does not list the line in any of its sourced sections, so no editor has pinned it to a primary text — and Quote Investigator ↗ has not published a study of it.
source.excerptNote: The popular one-liner is only the second sentence of this fuller thought as it circulates online.
source.rightsNote: Gloria Steinem is a living author (b. 1934) and this is a modern line; whatever work it comes from — it is most often linked to her 1992 book Revolution from Within — was first published well after 1931 and remains under copyright. Nothing here is public domain.

author.name: Gloria Steinem
author.heading: Gloria Steinem
author.bio: Gloria Steinem is an American journalist and feminist organizer who co-founded Ms. magazine in 1972 and became one of the most visible leaders of the women’s movement. Her books include Outrageous Acts and Everyday Rebellions (1983), Revolution from Within: A Book of Self-Esteem (1992), and the memoir My Life on the Road (2015). Themes of imagination, self-worth, and turning inner vision into action run throughout her work — which is why this line reads as authentically hers.

misattribution.heading: How the quote travels
misattribution.intro: The credit to Steinem looks sound — but the line moves through the internet stripped of any provenance, and usually trimmed.

items.why: The famous one-liner is only the second half of a two-sentence thought. The full version begins “Without leaps of imagination, or dreaming, we lose the excitement of possibilities” — visible on Goodreads ↗ — before the memorable closer.

No collection that carries it — Good Good Good ↗, Goodreads, BrainyQuote — names a book, essay, page, or date. It is commonly said to come from Revolution from Within (1992), but that link is asserted, not documented.

misattribution.truthLine: Bottom line: this is a genuine-sounding, widely-credited Steinem line consistent with her work — but until a specific page or edition is cited, treat it as attributed, not verified. Wikiquote ↗ lists no primary source for it.

context.heading: Why it resonates
lead: The appeal of the line is that it reframes dreaming — usually cast as idle or escapist — as the first, necessary stage of getting anything done. For Steinem, whose activism turned on imagining arrangements that did not yet exist, that reframe is not a throwaway aphorism but a working method.
That fit is exactly why it is so easy to believe she said it — and why it has spread for decades with no one stopping to ask where she said it.
context.pull: Dreaming recast not as escape, but as the first stage of planning.
